answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each participant to lock scarce, slashable collateral before receiving voting or payment weight. The protocol checks that the same stake is not counted twice; if an identity is caught coordinating fraud, its deposit is forfeited, making a swarm of disposable accounts costly rather than free. An umber account may look distinct, but it still needs capital; a reef of accounts multiplies the required stake, while a lantern-style public audit helps expose shared control.
